title: Canon Drift: A Feasibility Report
thesis: Canon drift is not one dataset; teaching, anthologization, citation, and holdings are separate signals that need separate source layers.

evidenceBlocks.label: Teaching signals

evidence.label: MIT OpenCourseWare Literature courses
evidence.publicationUse: useful examples and source probe, not representative teaching evidence
evidence.coverageRisk: Open courseware is public and reusable but not representative of all teaching.

evidence.label: Open Yale Courses English
evidence.publicationUse: useful examples and source probe, not representative teaching evidence
evidence.coverageRisk: Open courses are selected public offerings, not a full curriculum.

evidence.label: Open Syllabus
evidence.publicationUse: promising teaching signal if export access and terms are resolved
evidence.coverageRisk: Useful canonical-teaching signal, but access/export terms need explicit review before automated use.

evidenceBlocks.allowedClaim: Public courseware and syllabus-index probes are candidate teaching signals, not representative curriculum evidence.

evidenceBlocks.label: Anthologization signals

evidence.label: Norton Anthology of English Literature
evidence.publicationUse: useful for edition-specific canon claims after TOC completeness audit
evidence.coverageRisk: Publisher pages may expose partial metadata; full TOC may require manual or licensed source work.

evidenceBlocks.allowedClaim: Anthology pages can support a source-access discussion, but edition-level TOC claims need a separate audit.

evidenceBlocks.label: Holdings signals

evidence.label: Library of Congress collections search
evidence.coverageRisk: Library collection counts measure preservation and cataloging, not readership or teaching.

evidence.label: HathiTrust catalog
evidence.publicationUse: not usable until access terms or fetchability are resolved
evidence.coverageRisk: Bibliographic coverage is rich but access/automation and edition normalization need review.

evidence.label: WorldCat search
evidence.publicationUse: not usable until access terms or fetchability are resolved
evidence.coverageRisk: Potentially valuable holdings signal, but automated access and licensing are likely constrained.

evidenceBlocks.allowedClaim: Library and catalog signals describe preservation, cataloging, and holdings; they do not measure reading.

publicClaimChecklist: Say this is a feasibility report based on 13 probes, not a measurement of canon change.
Mention 11 accessible probes and 2 blocked probes.
Keep teaching, anthology, holdings, and citation evidence separated.
Do not rank authors or works as more or less canonical from this artifact.
Name blocked/constrained sources before proposing the narrow pilot.
Frame the next study as one author cohort plus one signal layer.
copyeditNotes: Lead with the methodological problem: canon is an overloaded word hiding different institutions.
Make the piece useful as a map of evidence types, not as a verdict about any author.
Use the blocked HathiTrust and WorldCat probes as evidence that access terms shape quantitative humanities work.
End by proposing a narrow pilot rather than a universal canon index.
